facts.claim: Claude views images in patches instead of pixels: each patch is a 28 × 28-pixel block, one visual token, so an image costs ⌈width / 28⌉ × ⌈height / 28⌉ tokens.
Anthropic’s worked example: a 1000 × 1000 px image is not resized and costs 1,296 visual tokens.
Claude 4.7 and later models are on the high-resolution tier: a long edge of at most 2,576 px and at most 4,784 visual tokens per image.
Other Claude models are on the standard tier: a long edge of at most 1,568 px and at most 1,568 visual tokens per image.
An image over either limit is scaled down, keeping its shape, to the largest size that fits both. For nearly all photos and screenshots the token limit decides the size, not the edge limit.
Anthropic advises that important text in an image should be legible and not too small, and warns that resizing a large image can make its text less legible.
Anthropic’s listed limitations: Claude may make mistakes on low-quality, rotated or very small images (under 200 pixels).
OpenAI counts some models’ image input in 32 × 32 px patches, ⌈width / 32⌉ × ⌈height / 32⌉, scaled down when an image goes over the model’s patch budget.

The 2020 paper “An Image is Worth 16x16 Words” showed that a plain transformer applied directly to sequences of image patches can classify images very well: the idea behind cutting a picture into patches.
OCRBench, a 2023 study of large multimodal models reading text, found weak spots in multilingual text, handwritten text, non-semantic text and mathematical expressions.
OWASP lists multimodal injection under prompt injection: an attacker hides instructions in an image that accompanies harmless text, and the hidden prompt changes what the model does.
Berghaus et al. (2025) graded eight multimodal models on invoices field by field and found the bank account number (IBAN) on clean invoices came out far worse than every other field.

Gurari et al. (2018) found that 28.63% of the questions blind people asked about their own photos could not be answered from the photo, often because it was blurry, badly lit or missed the thing asked about.
Anthropic’s vision docs (checked 2026-10-30): at Claude Opus 5.5’s $4 per million input tokens, a 1000 × 1000 px image costs about $5.18 per thousand images, and a 4K image about $19.14.

In Berghaus et al.’s (2025) test on clean invoices, their text-first route (a small model that turns the page into text, not plain OCR) scored about 10 points lower than sending the image for five of eight models: 85.1% against 96.5% for Gemini 2.5 Pro.
